title: Generics, Constraints & Polymorphic Function Signatures
summary: Learn generic functions, classes, and interfaces; enforce type constraints with extends; and implement polymorphic type parameters.
learningObjectives: Author reusable generic data structures (caches, queues, repositories) that preserve element types
Constrain generic parameters using the extends keyword to ensure required properties exist

sections.heading: 1. Generic Type Parameters & Generic Constraints
sections.content:
Generics allow functions, interfaces, and classes to be parameterized by types, enabling maximum code reuse while maintaining 100% type safety without resorting to `any`.

Without Generics:
`function identity(arg: any): any` loses all type information (passing a string returns `any`, losing string autocomplete and safety).

With Generics:
`function identity<T>(arg: T): T` captures the exact type passed by the caller and returns it identically.

Generic Constraints (`extends`):
Often, generic code requires the type parameter to satisfy certain minimum criteria (e.g. having an `.id` property). Using `T extends Constraint` restricts accepted types:

```typescript
interface Identifiable {
  id: string;
}

function findById<T extends Identifiable>(items: T[], targetId: string): T | undefined {
  return items.find(item => item.id === targetId);
}
```
Here, `T` can be any object (User, Order, Product), but the compiler guarantees that `item.id` is safe to read.

The `keyof` Operator:
`keyof T` produces a union of all property names of type `T`:
`type UserKeys = keyof { id: string; name: string }` -> `'id' | 'name'`.

Combining `keyof` with generics enables type-safe property lookups:
`function getProperty<T, K extends keyof T>(obj: T, key: K): T[K]`
This guarantees that typos in property names trigger instant compiler errors!

codeExamples.code:
+-------------------------------------------------------------------+
| GENERIC CONSTRAINTS & TYPE-SAFE PROPERTY LOOKUP                   |
|                                                                   |
|  function getProp<T, K extends keyof T>(obj: T, key: K): T[K]     |
|                                                                   |
|  const user = { id: "U1", age: 30 };                              |
|                                                                   |
|  getProp(user, "age")  ===> Returns number (Safe & autocompleted!)|
|  getProp(user, "typo") ===> COMPILER ERROR: "typo" is not in      |
|                             keyof { id: string; age: number }     |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------+
codeExamples.explanation: Generic constraints restrict type parameters, while keyof ensures keys exist on the target object.

keyPoints: Generics capture and propagate types dynamically without losing type information.
Use 'T extends Shape' to constrain generics to types containing required properties.
Combine 'K extends keyof T' and indexed access 'T[K]' for 100% type-safe property getters.
commonMistakes: Over-complicating signatures with unnecessary generics when a plain interface parameter suffices.
Using 'any' inside generic implementations, breaking type propagation to callers.

sections.heading: 2. Production-Grade In-Memory Generic Repository
sections.content: Enterprise data access layers frequently implement the Repository Pattern. Authoring a generic repository class allows teams to share CRUD logic across dozens of database entities while guaranteeing type-safe returns.

codeExamples.explanation: Demonstrates a generic entity repository with constraints on BaseEntity and type-safe property filtering via keyof T and T[K].

keyPoints: T extends BaseEntity guarantees that any stored object contains .id and .createdAt.
findByProperty prevents querying on invalid property names or mismatched value types at compile time.
commonMistakes: Allowing generic types to fall back to 'any' by omitting explicit constraints.

exercises.title: Build a Generic Result<T, E> Monad Container
exercises.objective: Implement a generic Result container to represent successes and errors without throwing exceptions.
exercises.description: Create a Result<T, E> discriminated union: `{ ok: true; value: T }` and `{ ok: false; error: E }`. Implement helper factory functions ok(val: T) and err(error: E), plus a map<T, U, E>(result: Result<T, E>, fn: (val: T) => U): Result<U, E> utility.
instructions: Write ok<T>(value: T) and err<E>(error: E) constructor helpers.
hints: `function map<T, U, E>(res: Result<T, E>, fn: (val: T) => U): Result<U, E> { if (res.ok) return ok(fn(res.value)); return res; }`.
exercises.submissionRequirements: Complete all checklist items, test assumptions, and document verification rationale.
evaluationCriteria: Addresses the root architectural/technical challenge accurately
Follows defensive industry standards and edge-case validation
exercises.solutionExplanation: Generic Result monads replace dangerous try/catch exceptions with explicit, compiler-enforced error handling.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: What does the expression 'K extends keyof T' signify in a TypeScript generic function signature?

options.text: That K is a numeric index array.
That K must be a valid property name (key) belonging to type T.
That K inherits all methods from class T.
That K converts type T into a string.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: 'keyof T' generates the union of keys of T; 'K extends keyof T' constrains K to strictly those valid key names.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: Why is 'function wrap<T>(item: T): T' superior to 'function wrap(item: any): any'?

options.text: Generics compile directly into C++ structs.
Generics preserve the specific input type, retaining autocomplete and type validation for the caller.
Generics make the function run asynchronously.
Generics encrypt the input parameter in memory.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: 'any' silences the compiler and discards type tracking, whereas generics capture and propagate the exact type forward.

recap: Generics provide reusable, type-safe abstractions. Constrain generics with 'extends' and combine with 'keyof' for complete property safety.
